business_summary.text: The Company is the largest single coal producing company in India in terms of production in Fiscal 2026, accounting for 21.0% of domestic coal production (source: CRISIL Report).

Its primary product is non-coking coal, including washed / beneficiated coal, supplied to power utilities, captive power plants, independent power producers and non-power industries such as cement and sponge iron.

The Company is a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India Limited, was incorporated on April 3, 1992 by carving out of South Eastern Coalfields Limited, and holds Miniratna Category I status; it accounted for 28.4% of Coal India Limited's total coal production in Fiscal 2026.

Coal production rose from 206.10 million tonnes in Fiscal 2024 to 218.31 million tonnes in Fiscal 2026; it operates 17 mines (14 opencast and 3 underground) in the Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields, Odisha, plus one 10 MTPA washery.
Long-term Fuel Supply Agreements accounted for 82.12% of revenue from sale of products in Fiscal 2026, and its customers are spread across 16 states in India.

concentration.text: Top 10 customers accounted for 51.95%, 58.04%, 55.94%, 55.71% and 53.30% of revenue from operations in the six months ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025 and Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
Top customer accounted for 12.45% of revenue from operations in the six months ended September 30, 2026 and 14.64% in Fiscal 2026; top 5 customers accounted for 38.06% and 41.09%, respectively.
Revenue from government-owned and controlled power generation companies and utilities was 41.68%, 47.64%, 44.81%, 47.53% and 41.89% of revenue from operations across the periods presented.
Sale of raw non-coking coal accounted for 97.38%, 97.13%, 97.41%, 97.10% and 99.94% of sale of products across the periods presented.
Sales to the thermal power sector (State, Central GENCO and IPPs) were 69.64%, 70.35%, 68.62%, 70.60% and 69.41% of sale of products across the periods presented.
Top 10 contractors accounted for 63.61%, 56.38%, 60.02%, 47.83% and 42.62% of contractual expenses across the periods presented.

Five of the top 10 customers for the six months ended September 30, 2026 have coastal thermal plants in their portfolio, and five are government-owned and controlled power generation companies and utilities.
Operations are concentrated in the Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields, Odisha: of 335.09 square kilometres of land held, 167.37 sq km is in Talcher and 165.96 sq km is in Ib Valley.

industry.text: Demand for non-coking coal in India increased from 1,112 million tonnes in Fiscal 2025 to 1,186 million tonnes in Fiscal 2026, and is projected to reach 1,564 million tonnes in Fiscal 2036 (source: CRISIL Report).

Thermal power accounts for approximately 70% of India's electricity generation in Fiscal 2026; coal demand from power plants was 698 million tonnes in Fiscal 2025 and is expected to reach 843 million tonnes by Fiscal 2031 (source: CRISIL Report).

After Fiscal 2036, demand for non-coking coal may decline; power sector demand is projected to fall from 934.40 million tonnes in Fiscal 2035 to 927.80 million tonnes in Fiscal 2038 (source: CRISIL Report).
Under a net zero pathway, coal demand is projected to peak at approximately 1.83 billion tonnes in 2050 and decline to about 161 million tonnes by 2070 (NITI Aayog scenarios cited in CRISIL Report).
Domestic coal output reached 1.05 billion tonnes in Fiscal 2025 and is projected to remain above 1 billion tonnes in Fiscal 2026.

Coal India Limited is the largest coal producing company in the world, with production of 768.19 MT in Fiscal 2026, and accounted for 73.8% of domestic coal production on a consolidated basis (source: CRISIL Report).

promoters.name: President of India, acting through the Ministry of Coal, Government of India
promoters.background: Individual Promoter; holds Nil pre-Offer equity shares in the Company. Promoter Group disclosures for this Promoter have not been provided.

promoters.name: Coal India Limited
promoters.background: Corporate Promoter holding 6,618,363,000 equity shares (100.00%) pre-Offer. It is a listed 'Maharatna' central public sector enterprise, incorporated June 14, 1973 as Coal Mines Authority Limited and engaged in production and marketing of coal; its promoter holds 61.13% as of September 30, 2026.

strengths.text: It is the largest single coal producing company in India (21.00% of domestic coal production in Fiscal 2026), with audited JORC reserves of 9,840.31 MT as at April 1, 2026, which would sustain around 45 years of production at current levels.
Its allocated blocks hold an estimated coal resource of approximately 40.34 billion tonnes as per ISP Guidelines, which is 9.80% of India's total coal resource.
It benefits from the strategic support and resources of Coal India Limited, including CMPDIL support for exploration, mine planning and R&D.

It runs low-cost, mechanised opencast operations, with surface miners accounting for 99.37% of production and the lowest production cost per tonne among Coal India Limited's subsidiaries in Fiscal 2026.
Its output per manshift was 30.34 tonnes in Fiscal 2026, 2.4 times that of Coal India Limited on a consolidated basis.
Its evacuation network is increasingly rail-led: railways carried 96.86% of first-mile-connectivity dispatch and 65.28% of total dispatch in Fiscal 2026, and it has access to five ports.

risks.title: Dependence on raw non-coking coal and long-term demand decline
risks.detail: Raw non-coking coal was 97.38% of sale of products in the six months ended September 30, 2026. CRISIL projects that non-coking coal demand may decline after Fiscal 2036 as renewables grow.

risks.title: Dependence on the thermal power sector
risks.detail: Sales to the thermal power sector were 69.64% of sale of products in the six months ended September 30, 2026. Sales to the power sector fell 4.82% to ₹ 204,854.09 million in Fiscal 2026, attributed to a higher renewable contribution.

risks.title: Government utility customers and delayed receivables
risks.detail: Government-owned power utilities contributed 41.68% of revenue from operations in the six months ended September 30, 2026. Payments were delayed from Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corporation Limited (₹19,298.80 million) and Andhra Pradesh Power Development Company Limited (₹5,021.60 million) as at September 30, 2026.

risks.title: Large unprovided contingent liabilities
risks.detail: Contingent liabilities were ₹ 125,132.90 million, or 55.86% of Net Worth, as at September 30, 2026, and have not been provided for.

risks.title: Dependence on Coal India Limited and conflicts of interest
risks.detail: The Company is wholly owned by Coal India Limited and its executive employees are seconded from Coal India Limited on terms that may be altered at any time. Other Coal India Limited subsidiaries are also in coal mining, which may create conflicts of interest.

risks.title: Customer concentration and loss of offtake
risks.detail: Top 10 customers were 51.95% of revenue from operations in the six months ended September 30, 2026. Customers may cut offtake if they secure their own coal blocks or, for coastal plants, switch to imported coal.

risks.title: Reliance on third-party contractors
risks.detail: Contractual expenses were ₹ 68,236.20 million (22.34% of revenue from operations) in Fiscal 2026. Top 10 contractors were 63.61% of contractual expenses in the six months ended September 30, 2026.

risks.title: Hazardous operations and inadequate insurance
risks.detail: There were 13 fatal accident cases between April 1, 2023 and September 30, 2026. The Company does not maintain insurance coverage in accordance with applicable industry standards.

contingent_liabilities.text: Total contingent liabilities were ₹ 125,132.90 million as at September 30, 2026, which is 55.86% of Net Worth of ₹ 223,998.03 million.

Total contingent liabilities were ₹ 85,062.30 million (39.80% of Net Worth) as at March 31, 2026, ₹ 101,222.10 million (55.18%) as at March 31, 2025 and ₹ 99,232.40 million (61.56%) as at March 31, 2024.
Income tax contingent liabilities were ₹ 80,748.30 million as at September 30, 2026, compared with ₹ 49,957.40 million as at March 31, 2026.
Water tax contingent liabilities were ₹ 8,573.80 million as at September 30, 2026; the State Government and Local Authorities sub-total was ₹ 19,298.80 million.
Miscellaneous land compensation and others were ₹ 21,010.00 million as at September 30, 2026, compared with ₹ 299.50 million as at March 31, 2024.

Demand notices of ₹28,640.70 million alleging production in excess of Environmental Clearance limits are under revision before the Coal Tribunal and have not been treated as a contingent liability, as outflow is considered remote.

related_party.text: Net amount receivable from Coal India Limited was ₹ 562.50 million (0.35% of revenue from operations) for the six months ended September 30, 2026; net amount payable was ₹ 432.80 million in Fiscal 2026.
Executive employees are seconded from Coal India Limited; the Company pays their salaries and these are not reimbursed by Coal India Limited.
CMPDIL, a Coal India Limited subsidiary and promoter group company, provides exploration, mine planning and R&D support under an annual work program paid through arm's-length contracts.
Coal India Limited is responsible for executive manpower planning, recruitment and promotions of the Company.
None of the top 10 customers are related parties.

red_flags.text: Payments were delayed from Andhra Pradesh Power Generation Corporation Limited (₹19,298.80 million) and Andhra Pradesh Power Development Company Limited (₹5,021.60 million) as at September 30, 2026.
Contingent liabilities not provided for equal 55.86% of Net Worth as at September 30, 2026.
Demand notices of ₹28,640.70 million for production exceeding Environmental Clearance limits are not reported as a contingent liability.
The Company does not maintain insurance coverage in accordance with applicable industry standards.
There were 13 fatal accident cases in operations between April 1, 2023 and September 30, 2026.

The Company's Chief Medical Officer was convicted under the PCPNDT Act (three years' imprisonment), the conviction was confirmed on appeal, and a revision petition is pending before the Orissa High Court.
An FIR under sections 286 and 304 IPC is pending against employees over the deaths of 3 individuals on site.
Research and development expense was nil in each period except Fiscal 2024 (₹0.50 million).
The CRISIL Report used for industry data was exclusively commissioned and paid for by the Company.
